Each specialist repeats all the adjacency bonuses of its tile and costs Food and Happiness (more each age), so specialists only go where a tile's adjacency pays for them. The plan counts on this share of each city's specialist limit on such tiles, so it gathers buildings with high adjacency on the same tiles. Towns have no specialists.
Also use unclaimed tiles within 3 of the centre that the settlement can grow into.

Plan this settlement together with your settlements and planned sites nearby (up to 5). Shared border tiles are split between them, and bonuses that cross the border (a wonder or quarters next to another settlement's buildings) are counted.

Estimate when each building gets built (production, cost, build order, unlocks) and count its yields only for the turns left in this age. A tile that only pays off later (next to a future wonder or quarter) is chosen only if it pays off in time.

Uses information the game normally hides: which wonders rival cities are building and how soon they finish (as Wonder Alert does). Off: only what you can know - wonders completed anywhere, rival wonder sites seen on your map, and the time left in the age.

Tier: what the wonder's effect is worth beyond its yields. S: free technologies, attribute points, a settlement limit, growth in every city; A: specialist limit, resource capacity, great works, celebrations; B: yields that depend on the map; C: small local bonuses; D: units and fortifications. The autopilot counts it when choosing among the wonders it can win.

After you place building tacks once, each recalculation replaces them by itself (no need to press «Place building tacks» again). Only tacks this planner placed are replaced, never your own, and never one whose building is already in the city's queue.

a building was finished or removed

Your tack at ({1_X}, {2_Y}) is on a tile this city does not own yet: pick that tile when the city grows. Click to show it.
Your tack at ({1_X}, {2_Y}) cannot be used yet, usually because no urban tile touches it: build the plan's buildings closer to the centre first. Click to show it.

Every new settlement starts as a town. A future city needs room and production to grow big; a town you keep grows to population 7, then sends all its food to connected cities (by road, or both on the coast of the same continent) and turns its production into gold. «Both» scores every site for both jobs and keeps the better one.
Best as a future city: settle a town here and convert it when it has the production.
Best kept as a town: grows fast, then feeds your city and specializes.
As a city: {1_City} | as a town: {2_Town}

Towns can only buy the Altar and the warehouses (Granary, Saw Pit, Brickyard, Fishing Quay, Harbor), so towns and planned sites marked «Town» get only those. Tick this to plan every town as if it were already a city (e.g. towns you will convert soon).

The Focus unlocks at population 7 (now {1_N}): keep «Growing Town» until then.
Not connected to any city: after specializing its food would feed nobody. Connect it first (a road built by a merchant, or both settlements on the coast of the same continent).

+{1_N}[icon:YIELD_HAPPINESS] ({2_N} buildings) and relic slots in temples

Recalculating the same plan with the same options re-plans only the settlements whose tiles, buildings, tacks, build queue or game numbers changed; the others keep their layout. A full recalculation happens anyway when an option changes or the plan is 10 turns old. Untick to always recalculate everything.
Adds this city's next {1_N} planned buildings (in the plan's order) to its production queue, each on its planned tile. Skips buildings already queued and tiles the game does not accept yet.
{1_City}: nothing to queue now (already queued, or the tiles are not usable yet)

When a city grows and the game asks where the new citizen goes, mark the best new tile by your priorities (green), the tiles the building plan needs, and the specialist tile that gains most (blue). The one that wins overall says «best choice». Numbers are value per turn by your priority; a specialist's is after the food and happiness it costs (the game's red numbers), which count for less when the city has plenty to spare and for more when it would run short. A tile where the building plan puts a building («a building comes here») counts only until that turn. The choice stays yours.
{1_Cities} cities, {2_Towns} towns; towns send +{3_Food} food to cities; {4_Lonely} towns feed nobody; {5_Growing} still Growing

Not connected to a city yet: connect it before choosing a Focus.
Show food network on the map

Map view: towns tinted by Focus (farming green, mining orange, other Focuses violet, still Growing pale blue, feeding nobody red), cities gold. Lines run from each town to the cities it feeds; labels show the food each city receives and each town sends to every city. Also in the mini-map's lens menu.
Switch between the large panel (wider, down to the bottom of the screen) and the compact one (leaves the minimap and unit panel free).
Growing Town, population {1_Pop}: it can choose a Focus now
Autopilot is ON: it acts at the start of each of your turns

While on, at the start of each of your turns the autopilot makes the decisions ticked in its settings with the game's own commands (it works online too). It moves units only with the options marked «moves units». It switches off when the game is loaded again.

One pass with the ticked options right now (F7), whether the autopilot is on or off; the turn is not ended. Only on your turn. Like the autopilot, it may reorder queues (wonders, units and walls first).
step not made: a pass is already running
step not made: it is not your turn
step not made: the AI plays your civilization
For stepping away (for example online with a turn timer): research, policies and other choices, production, growth, towns and purchases are decided for you; units move only if you tick their options.

When nothing is being researched, picks the next technology or civic. First what a danger needs: walls under a lasting threat or a war at your door, a stronger melee unit in a war at your door, Nuclear Fission in a war with a major with «Nuclear weapons» (and «Defence»), and Shipbuilding while a settler's only sites lie across rough seas. Then, ahead of the path's research when no slower than it: a node that gives a policy slot, a specialist cap, a syncretic choice, a city limit or a settlement cap you are about to reach, else one whose new policy cards beat the weakest ones slotted (valued by Policy Yield Previews when installed). With «Victory focus», the path's research (the way to the age's key research first). Else the game advisor's recommendation (the one matching your priority first), else the quickest. Future Tech and Future Civic only when nothing else is left, or when the path wants them. In an age's last turns, only what is done before the age ends.

When nothing is being researched, picks the next technology and civic: those giving slots and caps, and those whose policy cards pay, first, else the game advisor's pick; with the victory focus, the path's research first. Default: on.

A city whose queue is empty gets its next two planned buildings on their planned tiles; if the plan has nothing buildable there, the advisor's top choice (a building on the tile the game rates best, a project, or a military unit).

Fills empty production queues: the plan's next buildings on their tiles, else the advisor's pick; units and walls go to the front where a settlement needs them. Default: on. Wonders, the plan's tacks and its recalculation need it.
A grown city places its new citizen where the growth hints say «best choice»: a new tile or a specialist.
Places each new citizen where the growth hints rate best (a tile or a specialist), counting what Happiness does to the settlement. Default: on.

A Growing town at population 7+ that is connected to a city takes the recommended Focus; before that, its new citizens favour tiles that suit it (farms for a farming town, mines for a mining town). A Focus already chosen is never changed. While towns outnumber cities, or (with «Strategy by phase» and the science or economic focus) while cities are below the age's target (5 in Antiquity, 6 then 8 in Exploration), a town becomes a city: one founded on a city site first, then by the Towns tab's verdict, then with the science or economic focus the most production per gold, else the cheapest; after that, only a town the Towns tab rates «convert» on its yields. The chosen town is the savings goal: other purchases wait until it is converted. None with a war at your door, none in unrest, none for the age's target while a city is below zero Happiness (outside a crisis), and none in the final age's last 25 turns.
Sets the recommended Town Focus at population 7 and converts towns into cities by their production per gold, saving gold for it. A Focus already chosen is kept. Default: on.

Buy up to 3 planned buildings per turn, best value per gold first, then upgrade up to 3 military units the game allows to upgrade (those near a threatened settlement first), always keeping the reserve below. Towns' buildings (warehouses) take at most half the spare gold, and none while gold is saved for a goal.
Buys the plan's buildings with the gold above the reserve, best value per gold first, and upgrades units; repairs, walls and defenders under threat may use all the gold. Default: on.
Units waiting for orders skip this turn (they are not moved), so the turn can end.
Units waiting for orders skip the turn (they are not moved), so the turn can end. Default: off.
End the turn when done, so nobody waits for the timer. Not while the game still waits for a choice the autopilot does not make: the log then names it.
Ends the turn after the pass unless the game still waits for a choice the autopilot does not make (the log names it). Only while the autopilot is on; a step (F7) never ends it. Default: off.

Purchases keep this many turns of your gold income in the treasury, at most 1000 gold (late in the game a few turns of income would leave thousands idle). With a negative income: 10 turns of the deficit. The gold for a savings goal (a town conversion; with the victory focus, the path's next building) is held too: smaller purchases wait until it is bought. Repairs, walls and defenders under threat use all the gold. With «Strategy by phase» (and the victory focus) the phase sets the reserve for each turn instead (its tooltip in the strategy line); this setting stays as you chose it.
Purchases keep this many turns of gold income in the treasury (at most 1,000 gold; default 2). With «Strategy by phase» the phase sets it for each turn; your choice stays. Needs «Buy with gold».

Recalculate the building plan for all settlements this often (and at once after a building is finished, a tile is gained or new buildings unlock). Fast: only changed settlements are re-planned. Your building tacks are updated too if you placed them.

Recalculates the building plan this often (and at once after a building is done, a tile is gained or buildings unlock); only changed settlements are re-planned. Default: every 5 turns. Needs «Production».
Experimental: hands your whole civilization, units included, to the game's own AI for that many turns, then gives it back. Only in single-player games.
Experimental, single player only: the game's own AI plays your whole civilization, units included, for that many turns, then hands it back. Default: 5 turns.
The AI also moves units and may start or end wars. It stops after the chosen turns, one turn before the age ends (you choose the next civilization), when someone wins, or if you are defeated.
Not available in multiplayer: use the autopilot above.
Main hides the routine entries of every turn (units skipped or resting, the plan recalculated, tacks); Errors shows only what did not happen or holds the turn.
{1_City}: production queue empty, nothing suitable to queue
{1_City}: new citizen on a new tile (+{2_V}; a specialist {3_S})
{1_Town}: Focus «{2_Focus}» (an independent at war with us is near; only such a town can buy walls)
building plan recalculated ({1_N} buildings, {2_M} settlements re-planned)
the age ends next turn: choose your next civilization yourself
the AI was not started: the age ends next turn
taking back control: the AI plays one turn and hands the civ back
The game is playing your civilization by itself: an age changed during an earlier AI run, and the game saved your place as an AI player. «Take back control» asks the game to return it after one turn.

When a city's queue is empty, start the wonder the Wonders tab rates best for it: a race you are likely to win that finishes before the age ends, best value per turn of production (its yields, the boost to neighbouring buildings, and its worth for the culture legacy path and Tourism). At most this many wonders in production at once, each on its best tile.
Starts a wonder the city can win, by its tier and value per turn, done before the age ends, on the plan's tile; a race it will lose is cashed out into a building. Default: on. Needs «Production».
How many wonders may be in production at once (default 1). With «Strategy by phase» the phase sets it for each turn; your choice stays. Needs «Build wonders».

Makes the choices that hold the turn: empty policy slots (the card worth most by Policy Yield Previews when that mod is installed, else the first offered), the celebration bonus, story events (the option the game's AI prefers), a pantheon, a religion and its beliefs (worth most by Policy Yield Previews first), a government, a city-state bonus, the greeting for a newly met leader (friendly when allowed, else neutral), a leader's proposal (the cheapest answer that is not a rejection; never a rejection, which can mean war), "seen it" screens and advisor warnings. Espionage notices («Espionage revealed») are read. Great works waiting in the archive are put on display in free slots. An ally's call to arms is never joined (that is a surprise war, with war weariness): it is set aside, and declined (the alliance ends) only if the game still holds the turn for it. Peace (nothing given or asked) is proposed to every leader at war with you, every 3 turns.

Makes the choices that hold the turn: policy cards, celebrations, story events, pantheon and beliefs, government, city-state bonuses, greetings and leaders' proposals (never a rejection). Default: on.
Tick or untick every option of the group.
Switch every war option off (none is switched on from here: they are off by default).
only while the autopilot is on
if it was on at the age's end
«Strategy by phase» sets this value for each turn; your setting is used again when the strategy is off.
The generals: role, level and experience toward the next level; then the field operation under way.

Scouts head for the nearest discovery (cave, ruins, campfire...) within 4 turns first, even while exploring by themselves, then explore (the game's automatic exploring, else the edge of the fog). Cities train scouts first until you have 2. In the Modern age explorers dig up artifacts (ruins, natural wonders) and research new dig sites at your museums and universities; up to 2 are trained while there is something to dig or research.
Scouts go to discoveries and explore (2 are trained first); in the Modern age explorers dig artifacts. Default: off.

Cities train settlers (2 at a time while you have fewer than 3 settlements, then 1, never past the settlement cap; they go to the front of the queue). A settler waiting for orders walks to the best free site of the Settlements tab (searched by itself every 5 turns; the role that keeps cities and towns 1 to 1 first, else the game's suggestion), at most 10 turns away, and founds a settlement there; a town founded on a city site becomes a city when gold allows. Each settler gets its own site; no move may start a war. Settlers keep away from hostile military units: no site with one within 3 tiles, no way passing within 2; with one within 3, a settler stays in or runs to your nearest settlement (or steps away), even while walking; in a settlement it leaves for a safe site when its whole way there stays more than 3 tiles from them, else for another of your settlements with no enemies near. No site closer than 5 tiles to another player's settlement, nor within 3 tiles of an independent's village, nor within 6 of any village, friendly or not (founding there makes it hostile). A settler that has walked 12 turns, or changed its site 3 times, takes the nearest safe site. No settler is trained while no site is known. In the Antiquity age, below the settlement cap, no new wonder or science project starts: settlers first. A Migrant joins the settlement it stands in (Resettle; city or town), else walks to your nearest one, its citizen on the tile the growth hints rate best. In the Exploration age, until Shipbuilding, no land unit is sent across deep ocean (it stops on every ocean tile and takes damage there); coast is fine.
Trains settlers below the settlement cap and founds on the Settlements tab's sites (searched by itself), away from hostile units and villages; Migrants resettle. Default: off.

A military unit waiting for orders disperses an independent's village it stands on; else shoots (ranged units) at an enemy soldier next to your settlements first, then at other soldiers, the most damaged first (never at an empty tile, never a shot that would start a war); else heals when hurt; else walks onto an empty village at war with you within 4 tiles to disperse it (not a garrison; not while someone befriends it); else fortifies (or stands guard) where it stands. A melee unit (a fortified one too) attacks a hostile unit next to it near your settlements when the game's own combat preview says it clearly wins: the enemy dies or takes twice the damage it deals, and your unit keeps at least half its health; never an attack on a settlement, never one that starts a war. A settlement is threatened with 2+ hostile units within 4 tiles, or one within 2, or one within 4 while its centre is damaged (only independents at war with you count, and not a village's own units standing by it unless they are next to the settlement or attacking it): while it has fewer of your soldiers around it than hostile units, it buys its strongest melee unit at once with all the gold (towns too), the nearest city trains one first, soldiers away from it walk there, and a unit walks toward an independent we cannot befriend yet (stopping 2 tiles away). A settlement within 6 tiles of a village at war with you, with no soldier on or next to it, buys one with the gold above the reserve. One melee unit as strong as the best you can train is always kept: every settlement centre defends at the full strength of the strongest melee unit you trained, bought or upgraded in this age (20 with none). A threatened or exposed town still growing at population 7 takes the Fort Town Focus, the only way a town can buy walls, and then buys them. All defenders stay below 4 per settlement; the advisor's military units are only trained below 2 per settlement. While your gold income is below zero, no unit is added except defenders of a threatened settlement, and units are upgraded only there. When a unit shares a tile with another military unit (a new unit from the city), one of them steps to the nearest free tile, your own land first; boxed in by your own soldiers, a neighbour steps out to make room.

The army guards the settlements: soldiers go where the danger is greatest and strike raiders when the game's preview pays, defenders and walls are bought under threat, the generals stand at the worst fight. Default: off. The hunts and wars need it.

A merchant waiting for orders starts the best trade route the game allows, in the trade screen's order (most imported resources first, then the yields it brings by your priority). If the route cannot start where it stands, the merchant walks to that city first. One merchant per city, within each civilization's trade limit.
A merchant waiting for orders starts the best trade route the game allows, walking to its city first. One merchant per city. Default: off.
the turn was not ended: the game still waits for {1_What}
{1_Unit} goes to found a settlement at {2_X},{3_Y} ({4_Turns} turns)
{1_City}: queued {2_Name} (fallback: nothing the advisor offered could be built)
{1_Unit} stands guard (wakes when an enemy is near)
{1_Unit} steps to {2_X},{3_Y}: two units may not stay on one tile

While the autopilot is on, windows that only inform are closed as they appear: technology or civic learned, new unlocks, legacy milestones, age warnings, advisor warnings, wonder videos, tutorial messages, the turn-4 advisor choice, victory progress, the report of a rival's spy action; and story events once the autopilot answers them («Policies, celebrations, events»). Never diplomacy, confirmations or the end of the game.

Closes the windows that only inform (research done, unlocks, milestones, advisor warnings, wonder videos) as they appear; never diplomacy, confirmations or the game's end. Only while the autopilot is on. Default: on.
diplomacy: {1_Leader}, {2_Action}: left for you (only rejecting is possible)

Spends Influence to befriend independent powers, one a turn (the Influence pays for one): those threatening a settlement first, then those at war with you, then the nearest to your settlements (by their village); one you cannot afford yet keeps the Influence for itself. Once befriending reaches 30, its war with you ends. Under threat, more Influence goes into an ongoing befriending. Also asks civilizations for open borders when your explorers reach their land.

Spends Influence befriending independents, one at a time: those threatening a settlement first, then those at war with you, then the nearest. Also proposes open borders, starts reforms and incorporates city-states. Default: on.

After each recalculation the plan's buildings are shown as map tacks (Detailed Map Tacks); with settlers on, also the sites they walk to and the next best ones. Only the autopilot's own settle tacks are replaced.

After each recalculation, shows the plan's next buildings as map tacks (Detailed Map Tacks), and with settlers the sites they walk to. Default: on. Needs «Production» with a recalculation, or «Settlers».
Military explores (one garrison per city stays)

Military units other than one garrison per city go exploring: the game's automatic exploring if it allows, else a random tile at the edge of the fog up to 3 turns away, never into someone's land or a war. Fortified ones are woken for it; hurt ones heal first.
Military units other than one garrison per city explore (the game's automatic exploring, else the edge of the fog), never into someone's land or a war. Default: off.
{1_City}: {2_Name} taken out of the queue: the settlers you have already fill the room under the settlement limit ({3_Num} of {4_Cap})
{1_City}: {2_Name} moved to the front of the queue
Saving for {1_Goal}: {2_Cost}[icon:YIELD_GOLD] ({3_Gold}[icon:YIELD_GOLD] above the reserve so far); other purchases wait
Gold: {1_Gold}[icon:YIELD_GOLD], reserve {2_Reserve}; nothing to save for
gold for a town conversion on the next age's first turn (about {1_Cost}[icon:YIELD_GOLD] before the cards bring the cities back)
gold for the Modern Age (the age change keeps up to {1_Cap}[icon:YIELD_GOLD])
Gold reserve: {1_N} turn(s) of income (instead of «Gold reserve»)
Wonders at once: {1_N}, only those that grant Innovation (Great Library, Nalanda, Oxford…)
Growth first: food and production weigh most (plan, citizens, purchases); towns lean to farming
No settlers trained (one already on its way still founds)
Units upgraded only near a threatened settlement
In peace: none of the advisor's soldiers, and no military buildings but those that give production
Launch Pads in {1_N} cities: gold banked for them before Rocketry, all bought when it comes
A rival is near a culture win: one more wonder at a time, any kind (each one we build is denied to it), explorers allowed, resort towns, no Future Tech
A rival is near an economic win: gold is saved for gold buildings (GDP), no Future Tech
A rival is near a military win: settlers trained even in the final push (settlements count), no Future Tech
{1_Leader} leads ({2_Victory}): {3_Points} of {4_Goal} (×{5_Multiple} the second); we need {6_Need}

With «Defence» on. Off (the default) the autopilot only defends: it seeks peace whenever it can. On, in a war someone else started, it retakes a settlement of yours that the enemy holds within 10 tiles of your own: when your settlements are safe and no victory of yours is near, the soldiers the defence leaves free (at least 2 melee, 3 in all, 2 more than the enemy soldiers near it) gather 3 tiles from it with a commander, then ranged and siege units shoot its defences, melee units attack them when the game's preview says it pays, and a soldier occupies each district at 0 health; the settlement taken is kept. While that assault makes progress no white peace is proposed, and a peace that does not give the settlement back is refused; one that does is accepted. The campaign ends when the settlement is yours again, at peace, when your own settlements need the soldiers, after 25 turns or 5 without progress, or when a victory of yours is near. A commander leading it takes Initiative, Mobility and Regiments first, unless it already took a defensive promotion. Never a war of its own, never a settlement that was not yours.

Hunt the villages we will not befriend

With «Defence» on (default on). A village is hunted when we will not befriend it: a crisis encampment, one another leader befriends (not one already Unfriendly or Hostile with you), any past half the age, or one whose befriending your Influence does not pay for within 10 turns. Within 8 tiles of your settlements, when they are safe: the soldiers the defence leaves free (2 melee, 3 in all, one more than its soldiers near it) gather 2 tiles from it with a commander (the vanguard first), then war is declared on it, melee soldiers strike its soldiers when the game's preview says it pays, and a soldier steps onto the empty village to disperse it (100 of a yield, +10 with leaders near; the commander beside it gains the experience). It ends when the village is gone, after 15 turns or 5 without a kill, when 2 soldiers are lost with no kill, or when your settlements need the soldiers. Never a city-state, never a village you befriend.
Disperses villages within 8 tiles that you will not befriend, with free soldiers and a general (for its experience), when your settlements are safe. Never a city-state. Default: on. Needs «Defence».

With «Defence» on (default on). It starts when your settlements are safe, a commander reaches the raider within 3 turns and the free soldiers within 2 turns, with those packed in its army, are enough (a melee one, 2 in all, one more than their soldiers near it). It follows the raider while it stays within 8 tiles of your settlements, and ends when the raiders are gone, after 6 turns or 3 without a kill, when 2 soldiers are lost with no kill, or when a settlement needs the soldiers.

The autopilot steers toward one victory (culture, science or economy; never military). «Auto» picks it by the victories' own points: how far along the game's goal you are (once every race has one) and how far ahead of the best rival you met, with a bonus for close triumphs of that kind and, for the first pick only, for your leader's preferred victory. A victory switched off in this game is never chosen, nor science while your civilization may have only one city. The focus may change only in an age's first turns (its first 15%), once another victory has led by a clear margin for 3 turns; the final age keeps it unless your own countdown in another victory comes within reach. It then follows that victory's priority (Culture, Science or Gold: research and production advice, buildings, policies, growth, purchases); culture also builds one more wonder at a time. Close triumphs of that kind are ticked «Track». Its own work comes first, by age. Research that unlocks the path's work goes first (codex masteries and Literacy; Education and Urban Planning; Currency and Code of Laws; Industrialization and Mass Production). Science: a Library and an Academy in every city for codices (Antiquity); a University in every city and new specialists stacked on the urban tile closest to 40 total yield (Exploration); Launch Pads in your most productive cities (one is needed to win, more only where they bring the 100 Innovation sooner; each runs the repeatable Crewed Space Flight Preparation, 15 Innovation), an Airfield and a Radio Station in cities without a Launch Pad for the path's projects, a Schoolhouse and a Laboratory in every city, and every project that earns Innovation; once nothing of the path is left to research, the techs and civics that grant Innovation (Modern); cities buy these buildings with gold above the reserve too. Economy: growth onto tiles with a resource and, with «Merchants», merchants while trade routes are open (every age); a Market and a Lighthouse in every city for resource slots (Antiquity); settlers heading for the Distant Lands after Shipbuilding, for treasure convoys (Exploration); a Rail Station, Port, Factory and Stock Exchange in every city, factory resources into the Factories, and the Great Banker opening World Bank offices in other capitals (Modern); towns, then cities, buy these buildings with gold above the reserve, and while the path's techs are still to research the economy keeps science up. Treasure convoys always go home and unload. The tab shows the focus, each victory's points against the best rival's and its goal (Innovation, GDP…) and its countdown, the victories switched off in this game, and the close triumphs.

Steers toward the victory closest to winning (culture, science or economy) by the victories' own points, chosen in an age's first turns: research, buildings, policies and purchases follow it. Default: off.

With «Victory focus»: the autopilot plays in phases. Growth (the first quarter of Antiquity, up to its half while settlements are well below the cap; the start of Exploration while settlements are well below the cap or towns outnumber cities): food and production weigh most, so towns and cities grow and later build the focus's buildings faster; towns lean to farming; units may go ahead of wonders. Build-up: the focus's buildings and savings for conversions and the path's buildings; for science and economy no explorers, none of the advisor's soldiers and no purely military buildings in peace. Final push (the last age): settlers fill the settlement cap while settlements score (the military or the score victory switched on), else only below half the cap and none once the age's key research is 60% in; science banks gold before Rocketry for the Launch Pads the space race needs and buys them when it comes. Outside Growth, units are upgraded only near a threat. A rival near another victory adds its counter: one more wonder (culture), a GDP goal (economy), settlers (military), and no Future Tech. The phase sets the gold reserve and the wonders at once for the turn (your settings stay as they are); the tab shows the phase, its tooltip what it changes. Off: your own settings every turn.
Plays the focus in phases (Growth, Build-up, Final push); each sets the yields' weights, the gold reserve and the wonders at once for the turn. Default: on. Needs «Victory focus».
